title: FOV Calculator for Sim Racing: Assetto Corsa, ACC, rFactor 2, F1, RaceRoom
description: Free sim racing FOV calculator. Enter your screen size and distance to get the correct field of view for Assetto Corsa, ACC, rFactor 2, Automobilista, F1, EA WRC, RaceRoom, Project CARS and more. Single, triple and curved screens.
ogDescription: Correct field of view for 16 racing games from your screen size and distance. Single, triple and curved screens.
appDescription: Calculates the correct field of view for racing games from screen size, aspect ratio and viewing distance. Supports single, triple and curved screens.
tagline: The correct field of view for sim racing, from your screen size and how far your eyes are from it.
distHint: From your eyes to the screen center
bezelHint: Width of one side bezel. Used only for triple screens.
radiusHint: Listed in the monitor specs: 1000R = 1000 mm.
rigSvgAria: Top-down view: eyes, screens and field of view
copyHint: Click a row to copy its value.
how1: Pick your screen. Choose the aspect ratio and the diagonal in inches from your monitor or TV specs.
how2: Measure the distance. Sit in your normal driving position and measure from your eyes to the center of the screen.
how3: Describe the setup. Single or triple screens, bezel width, and the curve radius if the screen is curved.
how4: Copy the value. Find your game in the list, click it to copy the number, and enter it in the game's camera or graphics settings.
why1: The field of view decides how big the world looks on your screen. Too wide, and the track looks far away, corners come too fast and braking points are hard to judge. The correct FOV makes the screen act like a window: the car, the track and other cars appear at their real size from where you sit.
why2: It usually looks more zoomed in than the game default. That is normal for a monitor that covers a small part of your vision. To see more, adjust the seat in the game instead of widening the FOV: move it back, up or down until it feels comfortable.
q1: What is the correct FOV in sim racing?
a1: The correct field of view is the angle your screen really covers from where you sit. With it, the car, the track and other cars appear at their real size, so it is easier to judge speed, distances and braking points.
q2: What is the difference between horizontal and vertical FOV?
a2: Horizontal FOV is the angle from the left to the right edge of the view, vertical FOV is the angle from top to bottom. Some games ask for one, some for the other, and some use their own scale. The calculator converts the same geometry into the value each game expects.
q3: How do I measure the distance to the screen?
a3: Sit in your normal driving position and measure from your eyes to the surface of the screen at its center. A tape measure is enough; a couple of centimeters do not change the result much.
q4: What angle should triple screens be set at?
a4: Turn each side screen toward you by the Triple Screen Angle shown in the results, measured against the line of the center screen. Then every screen faces your eyes and the image joins up across the bezels.
q5: Why does the correct FOV look so zoomed in?
a5: Most screens cover a small part of your vision, so a physically correct FOV is often narrower than the game default. It shows less around you but makes speed and distances feel real. Many drivers get used to it within a few sessions. To see more, adjust the seat in the game: move it back, up or down until it feels comfortable. This only moves the camera, so the FOV stays correct.
